pronunciation: chok-ngit (the 'ch' is aspirated, like in 'church'; 'ng' as in 'sing')

example.romanization: Tshòk-ngit ngài hi sṳ-tshòng mai tshoi.
example.english: Yesterday I went to the market to buy vegetables.

note: In Hakka, 日 (ngit) is the everyday word for 'day', where Mandarin uses 天, so you'll hear it in many time words, such as 今日 (today) and 天光日 (tomorrow). Use 昨日 for 'yesterday' and 今日 for 'today'.
